artefact_criteria: thesis 004_method, sec:method:use_case_elicitation - BPMN 2.0 diagram with an explicit AI/LLM element inside the process
enumeration_method: ONE CENSUS OVER THE WHOLE HOST, THREE PUBLISHED INDEXES UNIONED. The population is the union of (1) https://docs.flowx.ai/sitemap.xml - 926 <loc> entries, the documentation platform's own sitemap; (2) https://docs.flowx.ai/llms.txt - 386 entries, the index this Mintlify site publishes for LLM crawlers; (3) the 11 https://docs.flowx.ai/_llms/* machine indexes the llms.txt points at (v4.7.x, v5.1, v5.9-*, release-notes and their sub-lists), which list pages by heading with their URLs. The union is 945 URLs - the 11 _llms indexes are inside llms.txt's own list, and sitemap.xml and llms.txt otherwise agree - and it is frozen in ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/population.json before any row was judged. NOTHING WAS NARROWED: no version facet, no keyword filter and no search box was used; all four published version trees (5.9, 5.1, 4.7.x and the 120-page release-notes archive) plus the 11 _llms indexes are in the population, and every row below is one of the 945. Every page's own published markdown was read (see access), so the AI terms could be counted over the whole population rather than over a search result.
access_method: docs.flowx.ai is Mintlify, so every page publishes its own markdown twin: appending `.md` to any page URL returns the author's own markdown (the site says so itself in llms.txt). All 945 were fetched that way - ledgers/_fx_fetch.py, about one request per second, 4 workers with a 0.4 s gap - into ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/pages/, and the 493 pages of the 5.9 tree and the release-notes archive that the site's own llms-full.txt bundle (14.3 MB) supplies were cross-checked from ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/pages_llmsfull/ (the two are the same published markdown). Screening was offline over that text: ledgers/_fx_screen.py (titles, surfaces, figures, AI sentences), ledgers/_fx_class.py (the dry-run classifier: 945 classified, 0 missing; E0 374, E1 535, BPMN-figure zone 36), ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/figmeta.json (all 3,965 figures of the 535 figure-bearing pages, with their alt text) and ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/fences.json (39 pages with a Mermaid fence, 24 with an ASCII sketch).
figure_method: Artefact test, applied offline to every one of the 945 pages' own markdown: an artefact is a standalone figure, a diagram fence (Mermaid; or a plain fence carrying box-drawing characters / arrow-node syntax) or a linked .bpmn model. 371 pages publish none (E0). 530 publish something else (E1, which names what it is: product UI screenshots, the vendor's own Integration Designer / Agent Builder canvas - 'Not a BPMN process' in this source's own glossary - Mermaid flowcharts, ASCII sketches, architecture box diagrams). 36 pages publish a BPMN-notation figure, identified by the figure's own filename or alt text (process_designer*, prs_def, bpmn*, pdm_process, delete_process, start_timer_process, process*.png): the 15 of those 36 that also discuss AI were each read and their AI mention dismissed by hand in E2_NOTES; the other 21 carry no AI/LLM term at all. The AI/LLM count is a census of a wide lexicon over the whole population, with two systematic false positives named and undone (the vendor's own name `FlowX.AI`, which made every page look AI-bearing, and the HTTP header `User-Agent`, which matched `agent`) - the same class of correction the processmaker census had to make for the word `model`. Images were used to confirm, not to discover: the 5.9 Process Designer's node palette was read by eye (15 tiles, ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/figures/sh_palette.png) and confirms the finding below.
key_finding: In this source AI reaches BPMN only by DELEGATION, never as a BPMN node type. The 5.9 BPMN Process Designer is genuine BPMN (pool/lane 'Default', start/end event circles, user tasks, service tasks, call activities, exclusive/parallel gateways, boundary events) and its 'Process Nodes' palette offers no AI node: only Start Events, Intermediate Events, Boundary Events and Activities. AI is bound into a process by an ACTION on an existing BPMN node - a Service Task (or Send/Receive Message Task) carrying 'Start Integration Workflow', as records 002/003/004 document. The AI-native canvases (Integration Designer, Agent Builder) are the vendor's own notation, which the source's own glossary calls 'Not a BPMN process'.
note: Read-only throughout: no login, no account, no form submitted, no captcha, nothing saved or deployed in any vendor UI; the browser was used only to read pages in my own tab of the shared Chrome (peers' tabs untouched). Pages were fetched over HTTP at about one request per second. No page of the population was blocked. CORRECTION recorded rather than rewritten: an earlier count in this session's dry run treated every fenced block containing `->` as a diagram, which counted JSON and JavaScript examples as diagrams (110 AI pages / 285 no-AI pages 'with a diagram'); the detector was tightened to Mermaid fences plus plain fences carrying box-drawing characters or arrow-node syntax, which is the 61-page figure quoted above. Two further false positives are named and undone in ledgers/_fx_build.py: `FlowX.AI`/`docs.flowx.ai` (the vendor's name matched `ai`/`llms` on every page) and `User-Agent` (matched `agent`).

artefact_criteria: thesis 004_method, sec:method:use_case_elicitation - BPMN 2.0 diagram with an explicit AI/LLM element inside the process
enumeration_method: ONE CENSUS OVER THE WHOLE HOST, THREE PUBLISHED INDEXES UNIONED. The population is the union of (1) https://docs.flowx.ai/sitemap.xml - 926 <loc> entries, the documentation platform's own sitemap; (2) https://docs.flowx.ai/llms.txt - 386 entries, the index this Mintlify site publishes for LLM crawlers; (3) the 11 https://docs.flowx.ai/_llms/* machine indexes the llms.txt points at (v4.7.x, v5.1, v5.9-*, release-notes and their sub-lists), which list pages by heading with their URLs. The union is 945 URLs - the 11 _llms indexes are inside llms.txt's own list, and sitemap.xml and llms.txt otherwise agree - and it is frozen in ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/population.json before any row was judged. NOTHING WAS NARROWED: no version facet, no keyword filter and no search box was used; all four published version trees (5.9, 5.1, 4.7.x and the 120-page release-notes archive) plus the 11 _llms indexes are in the population, and every row below is one of the 945. Every page's own published markdown was read (see access), so the AI terms could be counted over the whole population rather than over a search result.
access_method: docs.flowx.ai is Mintlify, so every page publishes its own markdown twin: appending `.md` to any page URL returns the author's own markdown (the site says so itself in llms.txt). All 945 were fetched that way - ledgers/_fx_fetch.py, about one request per second, 4 workers with a 0.4 s gap - into ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/pages/, and the 493 pages of the 5.9 tree and the release-notes archive that the site's own llms-full.txt bundle (14.3 MB) supplies were cross-checked from ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/pages_llmsfull/ (the two are the same published markdown). Screening was offline over that text: ledgers/_fx_screen.py (titles, surfaces, figures, AI sentences), ledgers/_fx_class.py (the dry-run classifier: 945 classified, 0 missing; E0 374, E1 535, BPMN-figure zone 36), ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/figmeta.json (all 3,965 figures of the 535 figure-bearing pages, with their alt text) and ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/fences.json (39 pages with a Mermaid fence, 24 with an ASCII sketch).
figure_method: ARTEFACT TEST, THEN EVERY FIGURE LOOKED AT. The artefact test was applied offline to every one of the 945 pages' own markdown: an artefact is a standalone figure, a diagram fence (Mermaid; or a plain fence carrying arrow-node syntax) or a linked .bpmn model. 372 pages publish none (E0-no-artefact). The remaining pages were then re-judged by EYE, not by figure count: every figure of every page that discusses AI or publishes an artefact was retrieved (1177 distinct figure URLs; 538 tiles tiled 4 per contact sheet at >=900 px in ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/sheets/) and each given one of the classes ui / drawn / bpmn-noai / bpmn-ai / unclear / broken, logged per tile in ledgers/flowx-ai.raw/visual-progress.jsonl (final tally: ui 392, drawn 59, bpmn-noai 87, no unclear, no broken, no bpmn-ai). Decision rule: a product-UI screenshot or recording is E1-not-bpmn with judgment:false (it is not a drawn diagram at all); a drawn diagram that is not BPMN - the vendor's own Integration Designer / Agent Builder / Workflow canvas, an architecture box chart, a D2 render, a stylised illustration - is E1-not-bpmn with judgment:true, and the note names what it is; a BPMN 2.0 figure with no AI node is E2-no-ai-element, with judgment:true when a real AI term survives the named false positives and false when only the false positives are left; a page whose only artefact is a fenced diagram is judged on that fence's source (Mermaid = a drawn diagram, judgment:true; an arrow sketch in text = a listing, judgment:false). Every row's judgment field, and the judgement-exclusion share the self-audit prints, come from this rule. CORRECTION recorded rather than rewritten: the first build named a notation from each page's figure COUNT alone ('product UI screenshots of the vendor's own screens') for figures nobody had opened, and produced 530 E1 rows that way; tools/audit.py rejects that, and the rows were superseded: 324 pages whose main text carries no AI/LLM term at all became mechanical E2-no-ai-element, 206 pages that do discuss AI were re-judged from the contact sheets (44 E1-drawn, 96 E1-ui, 37 E2-bpmn, 25 E1 on a fenced diagram, 1 E0), and the 3 pages that publish a Mermaid process whose nodes are BPMN element names and which contains AI task names became UNCERTAIN with records 008/009/010. Also corrected: an earlier dry-run count treated every fenced block containing '->' as a diagram, which counted JSON and JavaScript examples as diagrams.
key_finding: In this source AI reaches BPMN only by DELEGATION, never as a BPMN node type. The 5.9 BPMN Process Designer is genuine BPMN (pool/lane 'Default', start/end event circles, user tasks, service tasks, call activities, exclusive/parallel gateways, boundary events) and its 'Process Nodes' palette offers no AI node: only Start Events, Intermediate Events, Boundary Events and Activities. AI is bound into a process by an ACTION on an existing BPMN node - a Service Task (or Send/Receive Message Task) carrying 'Start Integration Workflow', as records 002/003/004 document. The AI-native canvases (Integration Designer, Agent Builder) are the vendor's own notation, which the source's own glossary calls 'Not a BPMN process'. THREE PAGES ARE THE OPEN QUESTION, and they are the ones nearest the thesis's artefact: https://docs.flowx.ai/5.9/ai-platform/tutorials/customer-onboarding publishes the entire onboarding process as a Mermaid flowchart whose 13 node labels are BPMN element names (four User Tasks, a Send/Receive Message Task pair carrying the edge label 'Workflow: kycVerification', an Exclusive Gateway with PASSED / FAILED-REVIEW conditions, a 48h timer boundary event, two End events); https://docs.flowx.ai/5.9/ai-platform/pre-built-agents/ai-developer and its 4.7.x twin publish a Mermaid graph whose endpoints are BPMN event circles and whose middle is a subgraph of four AI task names (Classify Document, Summarize, Identify process, Extract Prompt). Whether these count depends on the corpus's notation rule, so they are UNCERTAIN with records 008/009/010, not exclusions.
note: Read-only throughout: no login, no account, no form submitted, no captcha, nothing saved or deployed in any vendor UI; the browser was used only to read pages in my own tab of the shared Chrome (peers' tabs untouched). Pages were fetched over HTTP at about one request per second. No page of the population was blocked. CORRECTION recorded rather than rewritten: an earlier count in this session's dry run treated every fenced block containing `->` as a diagram, which counted JSON and JavaScript examples as diagrams (110 AI pages / 285 no-AI pages 'with a diagram'); the detector was tightened to Mermaid fences plus plain fences carrying box-drawing characters or arrow-node syntax, which is the 61-page figure quoted above. Two further false positives are named and undone in ledgers/_fx_build.py: `FlowX.AI`/`docs.flowx.ai` (the vendor's name matched `ai`/`llms` on every page) and `User-Agent` (matched `agent`). FALSE POSITIVES the census strips before counting AI terms, each named so the researcher can re-check the counts: the vendor's own name (FlowX.AI) and the host docs.flowx.ai; the platform's Kafka topic namespace ai.flowx.*; the HTTP User-Agent header on the integration pages; the ordinary words prompt(s), classification(s), retrieval, intelligent, intelligence, semantic, summarise/recommend, vector and the person-noun 'agent' ('Support agent needs to find customer's account'); model is deliberately absent from the lexicon (data model / process model are everywhere); and SITE CHROME, which puts AI words on every single page outside <main> - the header nav tab 'AI Platform', the nav item 'Using FlowX docs with AI assistants', the footer nav, and the disclaimer 'Responses are generated using AI and may contain mistakes.' - which is why the census screened each page's own markdown twin rather than the rendered DOM. EVIDENCE GAP, documented in OPERATOR-TODO P8: 8 figure URLs across 8 pages (n=103, 221, 285, 500, 567, 667, 674, 929) are S3 objects the vendor has made private (AccessDenied); no operator session can reach them, and those rows' verdicts rest on the figures that were retrieved. All 538 retrieved tiles were dispositioned; none was left unclear.
delta_vs_first_build: The first build's E1 rows named a notation for unopened figures. They were superseded (see figure_method) after opening every figure of the 206 AI-discussing pages on contact sheets and reading the fenced diagrams verbatim. Net effect on the verdicts: EXCLUDE 938 -> 935, UNCERTAIN 7 -> 10, judgement exclusions 62 (6.6%) -> 85 (9.0%), E1 530 -> 165, E2 36+324 -> 397. The judgement share is high because this source is an AI platform's documentation: after the mechanical re-code, what is left needing interpretation is exactly the pages that publish a vendor-notation canvas (E1 drawn), a fenced diagram (E1 fence) or a BPMN figure on a page that discusses AI (E2). It stays under the audit's 10% line; if the researcher wants it lower, the honest lever is the corpus's notation rule for Mermaid processes, not reclassifying rows.
